Existence philosophy quotes

Why this theme matters

This theme page collects 7 English passages that touch existence as a philosophical concern—whether as a concept to define, a value to pursue, or a problem to examine.

In the history of philosophy

Related discussions appear across Greek, Chinese, Indian, Islamic, and modern European traditions. Use the quotations below as entry points, then follow thinker pages for fuller context.

Thinkers in this collection

Søren Kierkegaard , Henri Bergson , Karl Jaspers , Erich Fromm , Jean-Paul Sartre , René Descartes

Frequently asked questions

What did philosophers say about existence?

They approached existence from ethics, metaphysics, politics, and lived practice. The passages below show several of those angles in compact form.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about existence?

This archive page is organized for that search intent: verified English quotations, with links to thinkers and related themes.

How should I read these quotations?

Read the sentence first, then check school and source. A quotation is a doorway into an argument, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

  1. Marry, and you will regret it; do not marry, and you will also regret it.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Proto-Existentialism
  2. For a conscious being, to exist is to change, to change is to mature, to mature is to go on creating oneself endlessly.
    Henri Bergson
    Intuitionism
  3. Man is always more than he knows of himself.
    Karl Jaspers
    Philosophy of Existence
  4. Love is the only sane and satisfactory answer to the problem of human existence.
    Erich Fromm
    Humanistic Psychoanalysis
  5. The self is a relation that relates itself to itself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Existentialism
  6. Man is a useless passion.
    Jean-Paul Sartre
    Existentialism
  7. I am, I exist—whenever it is uttered by me, or conceived in the mind, it is necessarily true.
    René Descartes
    Rationalism
